subtitle: Where a Queen Carved Victory into Twin Tongues of Stone

panels.shot: majestic low-angle wide of the completed Virupaksha temple towering above the river plain
panels.action: Queen Lokamahadevi stands in royal grace before the soaring Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal, the stepped southern tower rising behind her as the Malaprabha River and a cluster of other shrines stretch into the hazy Deccan distance.

dialogue.text: In Pattadakal, where the Malaprabha bends and dynasties met in stone, Queen Lokamahadevi raised Virupaksha, a temple of twin tongues, to bind victory, devotion and memory into one enduring form.

i18n.hi: प Pattadakal में, जहाँ मलप्रभा मुड़ती है और राजवंश पत्थर में मिलते हैं, रानी लोकमहादेवी ने वी रूपाक्षा उठाया—जुड़वां ज़बानों वाला मंदिर—जिसमें जीत, भक्ति और याद को एक ही रूप में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: broad aerial view of the Malaprabha valley at dawn
panels.action: The Malaprabha River glints in the first light as it curls past the rocky outcrops and scattered shrines of Pattadakal, with distant plumes of dust and flags hinting at a royal camp beyond the groves.

dialogue.text: In the eighth century, the Malaprabha valley was a stone workshop of the Deccan. Cave shrines, stepped towers and curving spires rose along its banks as the Chalukyas carved their gods and their power into the land.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी में मलप्रभा की घाटी दक्खन की पत्थर-कार्यशाला थी। गुफा-मंदिर, सीढ़ीदार शिखर और मुड़ी हुई मीनारें उठीं, जब चालुक्यों ने अपने देवता और ताकत धरती में काट दी।

panels.shot: medium wide on a cluster of early temples at Aihole and Badami suggested in the distance
panels.action: A row of varied shrines shows squat southern towers beside northern curving spires and flat-roofed halls, half-finished carvings and bamboo scaffolds revealing craftsmen at work along the rocky ridges.

dialogue.text: For decades, architects here had tested many forms. Dravida towers like those famed in Kanchi, Nagara spires from the north, and new Deccan experiments stood side by side, each stone a lesson in balance and form.

i18n.hi: दशकों तक यहाँ के शिल्पियों ने तरह-तरह के रूप आज़माए। कांची जैसे द्रविड़ शिखर, उत्तर के नागर स्पायर और नए दक्खनी प्रयोग, सब साथ-साथ खड़े थे—हर पत्थर संतुलन और रूप का सबक।

panels.shot: interior royal-court wide, slightly low angle on Lokamahadevi seated beside an unseen king
panels.action: Queen Lokamahadevi sits poised on a low throne in a Chalukya hall with heavy stone pillars, her face calm yet intent as courtiers bow and a scroll-bearing scribe steps forward from the shadows.

dialogue.text: Into this world of experiment came Lokamahadevi, chief queen of King Vikramaditya II. Her name would be cut into stone as patron, her will joined to the hands of many artists.

i18n.hi: इसी प्रयोगों की दुनिया में आई लोकमहादेवी, राजा विक्रमादित्य द्वितीय की प्रमुख रानी। उसका नाम दानदाता के रूप में पत्थर में कटना था, उसकी इच्छा अनगिनत कलाकारों के हाथों से जुड़नी थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Lokamahadevi listening to a returning messenger, focus on her thoughtful face
panels.action: Lokamahadevi leans slightly forward, eyes sharpened, as a dust-coated envoy gestures respectfully, a rolled dispatch bound with a royal seal held between his hands.

dialogue.text: Her husband’s campaigns had carried the Chalukya banner into the south, against Pallava Kanchipuram itself. Victories demanded memory, not only in songs and copperplates, but in structures that outlasted breath.

i18n.hi: उसके पति के अभियानों ने चालुक्य ध्वज को दक्षिण तक, Pallava काञ्चीपुरम तक पहुँचा दिया। इन विजयों को गाने और ताम्रपटों से आगे, साँस से भी लंबी चलने वाली इमारतों में याद चाहिए थी।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot as Lokamahadevi looks toward an unseen map or palm-leaf, candlelight flickering
panels.action: In the dim glow of oil lamps, Lokamahadevi studies a palm-leaf manuscript spread on a low desk, the faint outline of a temple plan sketched alongside lists of offerings and names.

dialogue.speaker: queen_lokamahadevi
dialogue.text: Let victory be remembered as worship, not boasting. We will build for Shiva.

i18n.hi: “जीत को घमंड नहीं, पूजा बनकर याद रहे। हम शिव के लिए बनाएँगे।”

panels.shot: wide shot of a council with architects; Lokamahadevi at center, low table strewn with miniature models
panels.action: Lokamahadevi sits cross-legged amid stone and clay models of temples, master builders kneeling around as they point out features of stepped towers and curving spires carved into the prototypes.

dialogue.text: At Pattadakal, she chose her field. There, among existing shrines, she would raise a great temple to Virupaksha—Shiva—offering the king’s southern victories back to the god who, in Chalukya eyes, guarded their line.

i18n.hi: पत्तदकल में उसने मैदान चुना। वहीं, बने-बनाए मंदिरों के बीच, वह वीरूपाक्ष—शिव—का महान मंदिर उठाएगी, राजा की दक्षिणी जीतें उसी देव को समर्पित कर, जो चालुक्य आँखों में उनकी वंश-रक्षा करता था।

panels.shot: close-up on Lokamahadevi’s hand hovering above two miniature towers, one Dravida, one Nagara
panels.action: On a polished board, Lokamahadevi’s jeweled hand pauses between a miniature stepped southern tower and a small curving northern spire, craftsmen watching her choice with held breath.

dialogue.text: The inscription would later praise her as patron, but the design drew on work already begun in the valley. Southern Dravida profiles and northern Nagara curves did not suddenly appear; they had been slowly married in Deccan stone.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख बाद में उसे दानदाता कहकर सराहेगा, पर डिज़ाइन ने घाटी में पहले से चल रहे काम से ही रूप लिया। दक्षिणी द्रविड़ आकृतियाँ और उत्तरी नागर वक्र यूँ ही अचानक नहीं उगे; उन्हें दक्खन की चट्टान में धीरे-धीरे जोड़ा गया था।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the temple site as foundation lines are marked out with cords and pegs
panels.action: At the open ground of Pattadakal, workers stretch cords to mark the temple’s base while Lokamahadevi stands beneath a temporary canopy, watching the grid form against the river and distant hills.

dialogue.text: She did not invent a style alone, nor summon some single miracle team from distant Kanchi as a tale. Instead, she gathered the living skills at hand, and gave them a clear, royal purpose and scale.

i18n.hi: उसने अकेले कोई नई शैली नहीं गढ़ी, न ही किसी चमत्कारी दूर-दराज़ Kanchi टोली को जादू से बुला लिया। उसने मौजूद जीवंत हुनर को जोड़ा और उन्हें साफ़, शाही मकसद और पैमाना दे दिया।

panels.shot: medium wide of ground-breaking ritual, with Lokamahadevi pouring water over a foundation stone
panels.action: At the center of a square pit, a dressed stone waits as priests chant; Lokamahadevi, head modestly covered, pours water from a spouted vessel over it while musicians watch in silence.

dialogue.text: Ritual set the first stone. Under mantras and drumbeats, Lokamahadevi dedicated the foundation to Virupaksha, tying her name to the base itself, so that later generations would know whose will had begun this mass of granite.

i18n.hi: पहला पत्थर अनुष्ठान से रखा गया। मंत्र और नगाड़ों के बीच लोकमहादेवी ने नींव वीरूपाक्ष को समर्पित की, अपना नाम खुद आधार से बाँध दिया, ताकि आने वाली पीढ़ियाँ जानें कि यह ग्रेनाइट किसकी इच्छा से उठी।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of the construction site bustling with activity
panels.action: The half-built temple rises as scaffolds wrap its walls, lines of workers hauling blocks, sculptors crouched over pillars, and supervisors tracing plans on the dust beside heaps of dressed stone.

dialogue.text: Years of work followed. Blocks were quarried, ferried, aligned. The garbhagriha took shape, mandapas extended, heavy stone beams bridged space, and every surface began to bloom with images from Puranic memory.

i18n.hi: फिर सालों का काम चला। पत्थर खोदे गए, ढोए गए, मिलाए गए। गर्भगृह बना, मंडप बढ़ाए गए, भारी बीमों ने खाली जगहें पाटीं, और हर सतह पुराणों की याद से खिलने लगी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on a sculptor carving a panel of a mythological scene
panels.action: A sculptor leans close to a stone slab, chisel poised as a scene of a god and demon emerges, delicate jewelry and tense muscles slowly revealed beneath his practiced hands.

dialogue.text: On its walls, stories ran like a carved river: battles of gods and demons, royal donors, processions. Each panel linked personal devotion to public memory, tying the Chalukya house into the very narrative of the epics.

i18n.hi: दीवारों पर कथाएँ खुदी नदी-सी बहती थीं: देव-दानव युद्ध, राजदाता, शोभायात्राएँ। हर पैनल ने निजी भक्ति को सार्वजनिक स्मृति से जोड़ा, चालुक्य घराने को सीधे महाकाव्यों की कहानी में पिरो दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle wide showing the rising Dravida shikhara over the sanctum, Lokamahadevi in the foreground
panels.action: The stepped, tiered shikhara climbs above the sanctum in carefully diminishing levels while Lokamahadevi, standing below, shades her eyes and looks up at the growing tower against a bright Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: Above the sanctum, the shikhara took on a distinctly southern rhythm, recalling Pallava Dravida profiles yet marked by Deccan hands. It signaled to the eye that this victory temple grew from contest with the south.

i18n.hi: गर्भगृह के ऊपर शिखर ने साफ़ दक्षिणी लय ली, Pallava द्रविड़ आकृतियों की याद दिलाता, पर दक्खनी हाथों से चिह्नित। आँख को बता देता कि यह विजय-मंदिर दक्षिण से टकराव से उगा है।

panels.shot: angled view emphasizing a Nagara-style curving shikhara of a neighboring shrine within the Pattadakal complex
panels.action: Near the main tower, an adjacent shrine in the complex shows a tall, gently curving northern-style spire rising in contrast, its vertical bands and amalaka-like crown catching the same sun.

dialogue.text: Nearby, at Pattadakal itself, Nagara spires stood in dialogue with this southern mass. The site became a stone conversation, northern and southern tongues speaking through towers, bases and halls to shape a distinctive Deccan language.

i18n.hi: पास ही, पत्तदकल में ही, नागर शिखर इस दक्षिणी भार से संवाद में खड़े थे। जगह पत्थर की बातचीत बन गई—उत्तर और दक्षिण की ज़बानें शिखरों, जगतों और मंडपों के जरिए बोलतीं, और अलग दक्खनी भाषा गढ़तीं।

panels.shot: medium wide inside the temple hall, Lokamahadevi standing by a pillar with inscription space visible
panels.action: Within the mandapa, Lokamahadevi stands beside a massive pillar whose smooth face has been carefully framed, a stonecutter kneeling ready with chisel, the empty plane poised to receive words.

dialogue.text: At last, the inscription was prepared. It recorded that Lokamahadevi, illustrious queen, had caused this Virupaksha temple to be built, dedicating it to Shiva in celebration of her husband’s victories over the Pallavas.

i18n.hi: आख़िर शिलालेख तैयार हुआ। उसमें लिखा गया कि यशस्विनी रानी लोकमहादेवी ने इस वीरूपाक्ष मंदिर का निर्माण करवाया और इसे शिव को समर्पित किया, पति की Pallava-विजयों के उत्सव में।

panels.shot: close-up on Lokamahadevi’s face as she hears the inscription recited aloud by a court poet
panels.action: In the dim hall, a court reciter raises a palm-leaf as he chants the new inscription; Lokamahadevi listens, her expression steady, pride and solemnity mingled in her eyes.

dialogue.speaker: queen_lokamahadevi
dialogue.text: Let them know I too stood behind this stone.

i18n.hi: “सब जानें कि मैं भी इस पत्थर के पीछे खड़ी थी।”

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot of the consecration, with priests and king implied, Lokamahadevi clearly present
panels.action: Around the sanctum doorway, priests scatter flowers and pour libations as the king’s silhouette stands at one side and Lokamahadevi at the other, the newly installed linga hidden within the dark inner chamber.

dialogue.text: Consecration joined stone and divine presence. As sacred waters bathed the linga, Lokamahadevi’s offering became complete: a victory monument transformed into a house of worship for generations of unknown devotees.

i18n.hi: प्राणप्रतिष्ठा ने पत्थर और देव-उपस्थिति को जोड़ा। जब पवित्र जल ने लिंग को स्नान दिया, लोकमहादेवी की अर्पणा पूरी हुई—विजय-स्मारक पीढ़ियों के अजान भक्तों के लिए पूजा-घर में बदल गया।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing the temple enduring across seasons and fading empires
panels.action: The Virupaksha temple stands unchanged while subtle cues show time passing—lush monsoon clouds, dry summers, small clusters of changing pilgrims—distant royal banners replaced by simple village life.

dialogue.text: Dynasties shifted, banners fell, yet Virupaksha endured. The temple outlived the very political quarrels that had inspired it; victory became background, worship the steady pulse in its halls.

i18n.hi: वंश बदले, झंडे गिरे, पर वीरूपाक्ष बना रहा। मंदिर उन राजनीतिक झगड़ों से भी लंबा जिया जिनसे वह जन्मा था; जीत पृष्ठभूमि बन गई, पूजा उसके मंडपों की स्थिर धड़कन।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot abstraction, hinting at present-day visitors before the ancient temple
panels.action: Silhouettes of modern visitors stand respectfully at the base of the ancient temple, their small forms dwarfed by the layered tower and richly carved walls glowing in the late sun.

dialogue.text: Today, Virupaksha at Pattadakal is honored as a monument of world heritage. In its stones, we still read how one queen’s patronage turned a moment of war into enduring beauty, speaking in twin tongues of architecture and memory.

i18n.hi: आज पत्तदकल का वीरूपाक्ष विश्व धरोहर के स्मारक के रूप में माना जाता है। इसकी चट्टानों में हम अब भी पढ़ते हैं कि कैसे एक रानी की सरपरस्ती ने युद्ध के एक पल को टिकाऊ सुंदरता में बदला, जो वास्तुकला और स्मृति की जुड़वां ज़बानों में बोलती है।

title_i18n.en: Lokamahadevi Builds in Two Stone Tongues
